# What is in the .exe, what you download after, and what is never shipped

*Generated by `python tools/parity.py` — do not edit by hand.*

Read this once, after installing. Everything in section A is already on your laptop the moment **ArcDeskSetup.exe** finishes. Section B is the short list of downloads, each one offered by a button inside the app, with its real size. Section C is what deliberately does not ship, and why — so nothing is "missing" by accident.

## A · Already inside the .exe — nothing to do

- **125 Python modules** of the app itself (`arcdesk/**/*.py`), collected by `collect_submodules("arcdesk")` in `packaging/arcdesk.spec`. A hand-written list is how a packaged app imports fine and dies on the one screen you only open once.
- `tools/doctor.py  ✔ shipped as data` — helper scripts the frozen app reads at runtime
- `tools/clone_speak.py  ✔ shipped as data` — helper scripts the frozen app reads at runtime
- the interface, themes, icons, and the generated in-app pages (HTML)
- `ArcDesk.exe` (the window) and `ArcDeskVoice.exe` (the ears) — two processes, so a microphone never shares a frame budget with the animation

| library | pip name | used for | in this sandbox | in the .exe | needed to start |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PySide6` | `PySide6-Essentials` | the whole interface | yes | yes | yes |
| `numpy` | `numpy` | audio buffers, image maths | yes | yes | yes |
| `psutil` | `psutil` | CPU/RAM readings, process list | yes | yes | yes |
| `PIL` | `Pillow` | screenshots, image edits, art | yes | yes | yes |
| `pypdf` | `pypdf` | reading PDFs at the moment you ask | yes | yes | no |
| `docx` | `python-docx` | Word files | yes | yes | no |
| `openpyxl` | `openpyxl` | Excel files | yes | yes | no |
| `pptx` | `python-pptx` | PowerPoint files | yes | yes | no |
| `mutagen` | `mutagen` | music metadata, playback info | yes | yes | no |
| `vosk` | `vosk` | the wake word (ears) | yes | yes — collected by the spec | no |
| `sounddevice` | `sounddevice` | the microphone | no | yes — collected by the spec | no |
| `sherpa_onnx` | `sherpa-onnx` | voice lock — who may command it | yes | yes — collected by the spec | no |

The build installs its dependencies one package at a time and prints which of `sounddevice / vosk / openwakeword / sherpa_onnx` made it in, so the answer to "can this .exe hear me?" is in the build log instead of guessed.

## B · Downloaded after install — from inside the app, one button each

| what | size | where it lands | where to press it | what it unlocks |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Speech model (Vosk) | 40 MB | `ArcDesk\vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15` | Settings → Voice → "Get the ears ready…" | the wake word "hey jarvis" |
| Speaker model | 30 MB | `ArcDesk\models\speaker_embedding.onnx` | the same button | the voice lock — only your voice may command it |
| Reply-voice engine · IndicF5 | 1.5 GB | `the app's own environment (%APPDATA%\ArcDesk\engine_env on the installed .exe)` | Settings → Voice → "Get the reply-voice engine…" | Tamil / Hindi replies in a cloned voice |
| Reply-voice engine · XTTS-v2 | 1.9 GB | `the same private environment` | the same button | English replies in a cloned voice |
| Built-in brain · Qwen2.5 1.5B | 1066 MB | `ArcDesk\models\*.gguf` | Settings → Local AI → "Add a brain…" | real conversation instead of Lite, offline |
| Built-in brain · Qwen2.5 0.5B | 469 MB | `the same folder` | the same button | a lighter chat-only brain for a small laptop |
| piper voices | ~60 MB each | `ArcDesk\voices` | the optional fallback voice (Tamil/Hindi/English, not a clone) | a real voice when no clone engine is installed |

**None of these are required to start the app.** Without them: the window, every tool, the vault and Lite all work; the wake word needs the two models (70 MB total), a cloned reply voice needs one engine, and a real conversation needs a brain. The app says which of those is missing, in words, on the dashboard.

## C · Never shipped inside the installer — and the route used instead

| thing | size | why not |
|---|---|---|
| torch + IndicF5 weights | ~1.5 GB | a compiled .exe cannot import a package that arrives later, and this would quadruple the installer. Installed into a private folder (or a sidecar environment) and spoken to through tools/clone_speak.py. |
| XTTS-v2 weights | ~1.9 GB | same reason, same route (CPML licence: personal use). |
| llama.cpp + GGUF model | ~1.1 GB | same reason. `llama-cpp-python[server]` runs from that same private folder. |
| your voice clips, notes, vault, logs | — | yours. They live in %APPDATA%\ArcDesk and are never uploaded anywhere. |

The pattern for all three: **a compiled `.exe` cannot import a package that arrives later**, and putting 1–2 GB of weights inside a 53 MB installer is not a product. So the app builds a private folder of its own (`%APPDATA%\ArcDesk\engine_env`), installs the engine there, and talks to it like a separate program. Nothing global, nothing on `PATH`, and deleting the folder only removes that feature.

## D · The parity check — sandbox vs .exe

| question | answer |
|---|---|
| does every `arcdesk` module ship? | yes — 125 of 125, collected automatically |
| does the build install every hard dependency? | yes (`PySide6`, on, a, laptop, pulls, it,, and, the, same, spec, then, produces`) |
| are the voice libraries attempted separately? | yes — sounddevice, vosk, sherpa-onnx |
| does the spec collect the wake engine? | yes |
| can a feature added later be added to an installed .exe? | yes, through the private environment; never by copying files into the .exe |

Anything in this table that reads NO is a bug, not a note. `tests/test_parity.py` fails the suite on it.

## D2 · Where the app writes, once it is installed

| path | what |
|---|---|
| `%APPDATA%\ArcDesk\settings.json` | every setting, saved atomically |
| `%APPDATA%\ArcDesk\vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15` | the speech model (B) |
| `%APPDATA%\ArcDesk\models` | the brain GGUF and the speaker model (B) |
| `%APPDATA%\ArcDesk\voices` | your reply voices and their transcripts |
| `%APPDATA%\ArcDesk\engine_env` | the private Python that holds a clone engine or llama.cpp (C) |
| `%APPDATA%\ArcDesk\vault` | answers, notes, the things worth keeping |

Copying that one folder to another machine moves everything except the enrolled voice lock, which stays per machine on purpose.

## E · First ten minutes on a fresh laptop

1. Double-click **ArcDeskSetup.exe** → Install → at the end tick "start with Windows, silently" if you want `hey jarvis` to work after a reboot.
2. It opens the setup card: pick **icon** or **voice**, read the five cards, press **Start ARC**.
3. Settings → Voice → **Get the ears ready** → 70 MB → the wake word works.
4. Settings → Local AI → **Add a brain** → 1066 MB → real answers instead of Lite.
5. Optional: Settings → Voice → **Voices…** to import a reply voice, then **Get the reply-voice engine** (1.5 GB Tamil/Hindi, 1.9 GB English).

Nothing on that list needs a command prompt, a key, or an account.
